# Street Fighter Arcade

Retro browser arcade with three competitive modes:
- `Typing Battle`
- `Code Clash`
- `Arcade Fight`

Designed for deployment at `https://sf-arcade.nealfrazier.tech`.

## Stack

- React + TypeScript + Vite
- Tailwind CSS
- Supabase Auth + Realtime
- Motion + Canvas Confetti

## Local Development

### 1. Install dependencies

```bash
npm install
```

### 2. Configure env vars

Create `.env` (or `.env.local`) with:

```bash
VITE_SUPABASE_URL=your_supabase_url
VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your_supabase_anon_key
```

`/.env.example` is kept in git as reference.

### 3. Run dev server

```bash
npm run dev
```

App runs on `http://localhost:3000`.

## Production Build

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

## Netlify Deployment

This repo includes:
- [`netlify.toml`](./netlify.toml) for build, SPA redirect, and headers
- [`public/_redirects`](./public/_redirects) for SPA fallback routing

Recommended Netlify settings:
- Build command: `npm run build`
- Publish directory: `dist`
- Node version: `20`

Then attach the custom domain/subdomain:
- `arcade.nealfrazier.tech`

## Social Preview (OG)

Social assets are included:
- [`public/og-image.svg`](./public/og-image.svg)
- [`public/og-image.png`](./public/og-image.png)

`index.html` includes Open Graph + Twitter metadata targeting `https://sf-arcade.nealfrazier.tech/og-image.png`.

## Git Hygiene

`.gitignore` is configured to avoid shipping local/private/generated files:
- env files (`.env*`, except `.env.example`)
- `node_modules`, `dist`, coverage, logs
- editor/OS noise and Netlify local state

## Scripts

```bash
npm run dev      # local dev
npm run build    # production build
npm run preview  # preview build
npm run lint     # type-check only

# 1990s Christmas Portal — Production Arcade

A refactored, modular take on the original tacky Christmas portal. The experience keeps every mini-game intact (snow console, reaction lab, present hunt, jukebox, theater) while adding a professional structure, accessibility, and performance-friendly effects.

## Project structure
```
index.html
assets/
  css/
    main.css            # global styling, layout, responsive rules, cleaned CRT aesthetic
  js/
    main.js             # entry point wiring controllers, settings, effects
    data/catalog.js     # tracks, vibes, movies, snow watchlist data
    games/              # individual game controllers
      snowConsole.js
      reactionLab.js
      presentHunt.js
      jukebox.js
      theater.js
    utils/              # shared helpers & state
      accessibility.js
      dom.js
      modal.js
      screenshot.js
      settings.js
      state.js
    effects/            # visual + interaction effects
      konami.js
      parallax.js
      snowfall.js
      webglGlow.js
```

## Running
Open `index.html` in any modern browser. No build step is required. Optional WebGL glow automatically falls back if unavailable.

## Key improvements
- Modular ES module architecture with reusable utilities and data separation.
- Production-quality styling with reduced duplication, responsive layout, and optional high-contrast mode.
- Settings panel for toggling snowfall, WebGL glow, and reduced motion.
- WebGL glow canvas (gracefully degrades) plus classic Konami easter egg.
- Accessibility: keyboard-operable ornaments, ARIA labels, and focus styles.
- Screenshot postcard button still powered by `html2canvas`.

# 757TECH.PRO

Astro + React marketing site for 757TECH.PRO, focused on AI automation, local agents, service landing pages, and blog content for Hampton Roads.

## Stack

- Astro 6
- React 19
- Tailwind CSS 4 via `@tailwindcss/vite`
- TypeScript
- Netlify-style form handling on contact pages

## Requirements

- Node.js `>=22.12.0`
- npm `11+` recommended

Astro 6 will refuse to build on older Node versions.

## Local Development

1. Install dependencies:
   `npm install`
2. Start the dev server:
   `npm run dev`
3. Open:
   `http://localhost:3000`

## Scripts

- `npm run dev` starts Astro on port `3000`
- `npm run build` builds the production site
- `npm run preview` previews the production build
- `npm run lint` runs `tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run clean` removes `dist`

## Project Structure

- `src/pages/` route files and landing pages
- `src/components/` reusable React/Astro UI
- `src/layouts/Layout.astro` shared page shell and SEO metadata
- `src/data/blogs.ts` blog post metadata and content
- `public/` static assets served as-is

## SEO Notes

Each routed page passes explicit metadata through the shared layout:

- unique `title`
- unique `description`
- page-specific `keywords`
- canonical URL
- Open Graph and Twitter image tags
- robots directives

Primary implementation lives in `src/layouts/Layout.astro`, with route-level values set in `src/pages/`.

## Brand Assets

Static brand and illustration assets live in `public/`.

Important files:

- `public/logo.svg`
- `public/og-image.svg`
- `public/linkedin-cover.svg`
- `public/robots/robot-coder.svg`
- `public/robots/robot-data.svg`
- `public/robots/robot-cloud.svg`
- `public/robots/robot-gears.svg`
- `public/robots/robot-wave.svg`

### LinkedIn Cover

Use `public/linkedin-cover.svg` for a wide-profile banner. It is exported at `1584x396`, uses the site logo artwork on the left, and places `TECH PRO` on the right for LinkedIn-friendly cropping.

## Content Editing

- Home page: `src/pages/index.astro`
- Contact page: `src/pages/contact.astro`
- Logo-to-site landing page: `src/pages/logo-to-site.astro`
- Success page: `src/pages/success.astro`
- Service landing pages: `src/pages/[slug].astro`
- Blog index: `src/pages/blog/index.astro`
- Blog posts: `src/pages/blog/[slug].astro` and `src/data/blogs.ts`

## Notes

- Blog card and article images should keep meaningful `alt` text.
- Inline robot illustrations are defined in `src/components/CartoonScenes.tsx`.
- Standalone robot SVG exports in `public/robots/` are better when you need reusable static artwork outside React.

readme.text:
# The Gazette Hub

A multi-brand, editorial-style news app built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.

The project lets you:
- Browse multiple newspaper brands with distinct visual identities.
- Navigate sections, full article pages, archive, and search.
- Configure brand styling (palette, typography, theme) from the UI.
- Edit article content in-app and persist changes in `localStorage`.

## Quick Start

Prerequisites:
- Node.js 20+ recommended
- npm 10+ recommended

Install and run:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Default dev URL:
- `http://localhost:3000`

## Available Scripts

- `npm run dev`: Start Vite dev server on `0.0.0.0:3000`
- `npm run build`: Production build to `dist/`
- `npm run preview`: Preview the production build
- `npm run lint`: Type-check with TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`)
- `npm run clean`: Remove `dist/`

## Tech Stack

- React 19
- TypeScript
- Vite 6
- Tailwind CSS 4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`)
- React Router 7
- Motion (`motion/react`) for page and UI transitions

## App Routes

- `/`: Home/front page
- `/article/:id`: Full article page
- `/sections` and `/sections/:name`: Section views
- `/search`: Search experience
- `/archive`: Archive page
- `/hub`: Brand hub
- `/config`: Brand and content configuration
- `/editor/:brandId/:articleId`: Article editor
- `/about`, `/contact`, `/terms`: Static pages

## Data and State Model

- Seed data lives in `src/constants.ts` as `MOCK_BRANDS`.
- Global state is managed in `src/context/NewspaperContext.tsx`.
- Brand data is normalized through `src/brandDesign.ts`.
- Runtime edits are saved to browser `localStorage` under:
  - `newspaper_brands`
  - `current_brand_index`

## Project Structure

```text
src/
  components/       # Layout, header, and article presentation components
  context/          # Global state provider for brands and publication data
  pages/            # Route-level pages (home, config, editor, archive, etc.)
  lib/              # Shared utilities
  brandDesign.ts    # Palette/font systems and design normalization
  constants.ts      # Seed brand + article content
  types.ts          # Domain models
```

## Customization Workflow

1. Open `/config` to adjust theme, palette, and typography.
2. Add or remove brands from the same screen.
3. Edit article markdown in the content editor.
4. Refresh the app to verify persisted local state behavior.

If you want permanent baseline content changes, edit `src/constants.ts` directly.

readme.text:
# Unthink AI

Unthink AI is a Vite + React app with a Netlify/Express API proxy that requires each user to provide their own Gemini API key per request.

## Local development

1. Install dependencies:
   `npm install`
2. Optional: create `.env` from `.env.example` if you need to set `PORT`
3. Start the app with Express middleware:
   `npm run dev`
4. Open `http://localhost:3000`

## Production deployment (Netlify)

- Build command: `npm run build`
- Publish directory: `dist`
- Netlify Function path: `netlify/functions/decide.ts`
- API redirect: `/api/decide -> /.netlify/functions/decide` in `netlify.toml`
- Security headers and SPA fallback redirects are configured in `netlify.toml`

## API request flow

1. Browser sends `POST /api/decide` with `{ prompt, apiKey }`
2. In Netlify production, redirect routes request to `/.netlify/functions/decide`
3. API validates prompt length (1-500 chars) and presence of `apiKey`
4. API calls Gemini using the user-provided `apiKey`
5. API returns `{ decision }`

## Environment variables

- `PORT` (optional): used by local Express runtime

## SEO assets

- Page-level metadata in `index.html` (title, description, canonical, OG/Twitter)
- `public/robots.txt`
- `public/sitemap.xml`
- `public/og-image.svg`

## Post-deploy verification checklist

1. Confirm canonical resolves to your final production domain
2. Confirm `https://<domain>/robots.txt` is reachable
3. Confirm `https://<domain>/sitemap.xml` is reachable
4. Confirm `POST https://<domain>/api/decide` returns JSON
5. Run Google URL Inspection on the homepage

## Netlify AI Endpoint

- Endpoint: `POST /api/decide` -> Netlify Function `netlify/functions/decide.ts`
- No server-managed Gemini key is used
- Users must pass their own Gemini API key in each request

│   └── pages/              # Routing structure (index.astro, about.astro, services.astro, careers, contact)

└── package.json            # Scripts and dependencies

readme.text:
# Vision Link: Face & Hand Control

Vision Link is a browser-based, touchless interaction demo built with React + Vite.
It uses MediaPipe face and hand landmarks to drive on-screen navigation zones and gesture-like interactions.

## Features

- Real-time webcam tracking for face and hands
- Nose-position zones for previous/next/select/scroll actions
- Dwell-based zone activation
- Optional landmark visualization overlay
- Netlify-ready SPA deployment config

## Tech Stack

- React 19 + TypeScript
- Vite 6
- `@mediapipe/tasks-vision`
- Tailwind CSS 4
- Netlify (static hosting)

## Local Development

Prerequisites:

- Node.js 20+
- npm

Install and run:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`.

## Environment Variables

This app does not require a Gemini API key for its core face/hand tracking flow.
If you add AI features later, use `.env.local` for local secrets and keep them out of source control.

Example `.env.local`:

```bash
GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key_here
```

## Scripts

```bash
npm run dev      # local dev server
npm run lint     # TypeScript no-emit check
npm run build    # production build to dist/
npm run preview  # preview production build
```

## Deployment (Netlify)

This repo includes [`netlify.toml`](./netlify.toml) with:

- build command: `npm run build`
- publish directory: `dist`
- SPA redirect: `/* -> /index.html`
- baseline security headers

Deploy steps:

1. Connect repo in Netlify.
2. Confirm build command and publish directory from `netlify.toml`.
3. Configure custom domain and HTTPS.
4. Verify camera permission prompt and tracking behavior on the deployed domain.

## Usage Notes

- Camera permission is required.
- Best results are in a well-lit environment.
- Keep your face centered for stable zone detection.

## SEO and Domain

Canonical domain target is documented in [`DEPLOY_DOMAIN.md`](./DEPLOY_DOMAIN.md).
The app includes `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, favicon, and OG image assets in `public/`.

# Blackjack Trainer: Count Lab

A training-focused blackjack app for faster card-counting skill development.

## What Was Added

- Upgraded round resolution:
  - Full hand outcomes (`win`, `loss`, `push`, `blackjack payout`)
  - Dealer reveal + dealer draw logic
  - Session stats (`hands`, `W/L/P`, streaks, bankroll)
- Freeze coaching popup system:
  - Pauses action during high-value learning spots
  - Explains the situation and recommended basic-strategy move
  - Resume button unfreezes play
- Audio system:
  - Toggleable ambient table loop (generated with WebAudio)
  - Action/result sound cues for feedback
- Quiz mode:
  - 120-question pool for true-count conversion
  - Each run shuffles and serves 30 questions
  - Immediate explanation after each answer
- Study guide tab:
  - Fast in-app reference for counting flow and discipline

## Stack

- React + Vite
- Material UI

## Run Locally

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Build:

```bash
npm run build
```

## Card Counting Method (Hi-Lo)

Use the Hi-Lo system:

- `2, 3, 4, 5, 6` = `+1`
- `7, 8, 9` = `0`
- `10, J, Q, K, A` = `-1`

### Workflow

1. Track running count as cards are revealed.
2. Estimate decks remaining.
3. Convert:

```text
True Count = Running Count / Decks Remaining
```

4. Use true count for bet sizing and discipline.

## Why Freeze Moments Help

Most new counters lose edge from:

- Rushed decisions on stiff totals
- Ignoring count context when emotional
- Over-hitting made hands

The freeze coach interrupts these leak points and forces one focused decision cycle:

1. See board state
2. Read recommendation
3. Resume and execute intentionally

## Quiz Details

- Pool size: `120`
- Session size: `30`
- Question type: true-count conversion under time pressure
- Goal benchmark: `80%+` accuracy

## Suggested Practice Routine

1. Play 20-40 trainer hands with freeze mode ON.
2. Run one 30-question quiz.
3. Repeat with freeze mode OFF.
4. Track:
   - Quiz accuracy trend
   - Wrong-answer patterns
   - Stability of true-count/bet decisions

## Notes

- Audio uses generated tones (no external audio assets required).
- This is a training simulator, not gambling advice.

# NULL AI Agent Framework

A local-first, multi-agent AI orchestration framework built for **Parrot OS**. 
Indexes, manages, chains, and runs 47+ AI/security/development tools through a unified Python CLI with support for **Codex**, **OpenClaw**, and **Hermes** agent backends.

## Architecture

```
NULL AI AGENT FRAMEWORK/
├── README.md                          # This file
├── tools/
│   ├── null ai agent tools/           # Main tool library (47 tools)
│   │   ├── local_null_ai_orchestrator/ # Central orchestrator
│   │   │   ├── orchestrator.py         # CLI — scan, list, run, session, chain, install, dashboard
│   │   │   ├── runtime/               # Python runtime infrastructure
│   │   │   │   ├── python_env.py       # Virtualenv & dependency management
│   │   │   │   ├── parrot_os.py        # Parrot OS hardware & tool detection
│   │   │   │   └── agent_protocol.py   # Standard agent interface protocol
│   │   │   ├── config/agents.json      # Agent backend definitions
│   │   │   ├── playbooks/              # JSON agent workflow playbooks
│   │   │   └── registry.local.json     # Auto-generated tool registry
│   │   ├── cybersecurity/             # Security & pentesting tools (11 tools)
│   │   ├── website generators/        # Astro/Vite site builders (4 tools)
│   │   ├── script generators/         # Automation & app builders (23 tools)
│   │   ├── media generators/          # Image/video generation (2 tools)
│   │   ├── design/                    # Design intelligence (2 tools)
│   │   ├── seo/                       # SEO intelligence (2 tools)
│   │   ├── social-media/              # Social automation (1 tool)
│   │   └── house-of-skills/           # Agent skill libraries (2 tools)
│   ├── potential ideas of services/   # Project catalog (~40 service ideas)
│   └── 100websitesproject/            # 100 Websites Challenge artifacts
└── 100 Websites in 30 Days/           # Quality audit & tracking docs
```

## Quick Start

```bash
cd "tools/null ai agent tools/local_null_ai_orchestrator"

# See the full system dashboard
python3 orchestrator.py dashboard

# Scan and index all tools
python3 orchestrator.py scan

# List tools with summary
python3 orchestrator.py list --summary

# See detailed system info
python3 orchestrator.py doctor
```

## Core Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `dashboard` | Full Parrot OS + tool health report |
| `scan` | Re-index all `local_null_ai_*` folders |
| `list` | List tools (filter by `--category`, `--runtime`, `--tag`) |
| `show <tool>` | Detailed tool information |
| `doctor` | System, agent, and runtime checks |
| `run <tool> -- <cmd>` | Dry-run or execute commands in a tool folder |
| `install <tool>` | Install Python dependencies in a venv |
| `session <tool>` | Prepare an interactive agent session |
| `chain --list` | List available tool chains |
| `chain --run <id>` | Prepare a chain of tools |
| `env` | Environment details |
| `assess` | Score tools and generate enhancement

# GhostBox Concierge — Hot App Summer Edition

Physical AI concierge for the **ESP32-S3 N16R8 + Lafvin Chatbot Shield**. Drop it on a coffee shop table, workshop desk, or storefront. Customers pick a question with two buttons; the gadget shows + speaks the AI answer and logs everything to a live web dashboard.

## What You Need

- ESP32-S3 N16R8 + Lafvin Chatbot Shield (TFT200C 240×320 + ES8311 audio)
- 2.4 GHz WiFi network the gadget can join
- A computer on the same network to run the backend
- Arduino IDE with ESP32 board support + these libraries:
  - LovyanGFX
  - ArduinoJson
  - ESP32-audioI2S (already in your lib folder)

## File Layout

```
~/Arduino/ghostbox-concierge/          # Firmware (open this folder in Arduino IDE)
~/hermes-workspace/ghostbox-concierge/ # Backend + dashboard
```

## 1. Configure WiFi

Edit `~/Arduino/ghostbox-concierge/config.h`:

```cpp
#define WIFI_SSID  "YourNetwork"
#define WIFI_PASS  "YourPassword"
```

Also set the backend URL if your backend is not on `192.168.0.25:5000`:

```cpp
#define CONCIERGE_SERVER_URL "http://YOUR_BACKEND_IP:5000/api/concierge/ask"
```

## 2. Start the Backend

In a terminal on the backend machine:

```bash
cd ~/hermes-workspace/ghostbox-concierge/backend
./venv/bin/python app.py
```

Open the dashboard at `http://192.168.0.25:5000`.

The backend defaults to calling Ollama at `192.168.0.20:11434`. If you don't have Ollama, set an OpenAI key:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
./venv/bin/python app.py
```

## 3. Flash the Firmware

1. Open Arduino IDE
2. Open `~/Arduino/ghostbox-concierge/ghostbox-concierge.ino`
3. Board: **ESP32S3 Dev Module**
4. Partition Scheme: **16MB Flash (4MB App / 4MB FATFS)** or **Huge APP (3MB No OTA / 1MB SPIFFS)**
5. USB CDC On Boot: **Enabled**
6. Upload Mode: **UART0 / Hardware CDC**
7. Port: `/dev/ttyACM0` (or the port your S3 shows up on)
8. Click Upload

## 4. Use It

- Boot screen → Home
- UP button → Main Menu
- Select **Concierge**
- DOWN button cycles 6 preset questions
- UP button sends the question
- Screen shows "thinking" then the AI answer
- Scroll answer with DOWN, long DOWN to jump top, UP to go back

Every question + answer appears live on the dashboard.

## Dashboard

The dashboard is in `backend/static/index.html`. It polls `/api/concierge/history` every 3 seconds and shows a live feed.

## Deploy Publicly

Use `render.yaml` at the repo root to deploy to Render, or host on any Python-friendly service. Set `OLLAMA_URL` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` as environment variables.

## Customizing Questions

Edit `conciergeQuestion()` in `ghostbox-concierge.ino` and `CONCIERGE_ITEMS` in `AppState.cpp`. Add as many as you like — the menu scrolls.

## Safety

This project is for authorized demos and your own workshops. Don't deploy rogue USB-HID or network tools without permission.

# Insane Visuals

A browser-based music-visualization app built with **Three.js** and the **Web Audio API**. Load an audio file, paste a YouTube URL, or enable your microphone and watch seven distinct reactive scenes respond to the music in real time.

## Scenes

- **Nebula** — 7000 glowing particles in frequency shells with dynamic liquid-web trails.
- **Liquid** — a translucent, iridescent blob warped by real 3D simplex noise, orbited by colored lights, with PBR environment reflections.
- **Trails** — smooth Catmull-Rom ribbons orbit the camera, colored by bass/mids/treble.
- **Waveform** — a shader terrain deformed by waveform and frequency data with rising beat particles and ribbons.
- **Crystal** — wireframe icosahedra scale/spin to the beat with per-crystal trails and connecting ribbons.
- **Magic** — rising particle fountain, rotating runes, and a pulsing ring floor.
- **Kaleido** — geometric shard galaxy + radial spokes + particle dust, fed through a kaleidoscope shader pass.

## Post-processing

All scenes render through an `EffectComposer` pipeline:

1. **RenderPass** — renders the active visualizer's scene
2. **UnrealBloomPass** — GPU bloom, strength/radius driven by live audio energy
3. **AfterimagePass** — screen-space motion trails, damp driven by the Trail Mix slider
4. **KaleidoShader** (kaleido mode only) — radial reflection kaleidoscope
5. **OutputPass** — tone mapping + color space correction

## Controls

- **Load Audio** — local file playback
- **Microphone** — live input (muted to prevent feedback)
- **Load YouTube** — fetch audio via the Netlify Function proxy
- **Reactivity** slider — amplify or damp how strongly the visuals react to the music
- **Trail Mix** slider — controls afterimage trail intensity + trail/ribbon opacity in supported modes
- **Vol** — playback volume

## Tech stack

- Vite
- Three.js (r165) with built-in addons:
  - `EffectComposer`, `RenderPass`, `UnrealBloomPass`, `AfterimagePass`, `ShaderPass`, `OutputPass`
  - `KaleidoShader`
  - `SimplexNoise` (liquid blob deformation)
  - `RoomEnvironment` + `PMREMGenerator` (liquid PBR reflections)
  - `OrbitControls` (all modes)
- Web Audio API / AnalyserNode
- Vanilla JavaScript (ES modules)
- Netlify Functions (`ytdl-core`) for YouTube audio

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the URL Vite prints (usually `http://localhost:5173`).

## YouTube audio via Netlify Function

The function at `netlify/functions/youtube-audio.js` resolves a YouTube URL to the best audio-only stream and returns a `302` redirect. `netlify.toml` maps `/api/*` to that function.

To test locally:

```bash
npx netlify dev
```

> ⚠️ Extracting audio from YouTube may violate YouTube's Terms of Service. This feature is for personal experimentation only.

## Production build

```bash
npm run build
```

Static output goes to `dist/` and can be deployed to any static host.

## SEO

- Per-page `<title>`, meta description, canonical URL, Open Graph + Twitter card tags

# StraightLine Desk

Internal cold-calling workspace for Hampton Roads business listings.

## Quick start

1. **Start the backend** (SQLite + Flask API)
   ```bash
   ./start-backend.sh
   ```
   Runs on `http://127.0.0.1:8420`

2. **Start the frontend**
   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```
   Opens on `http://localhost:4173`

## Backend

- `backend/main.py` — Flask API serving listings, opportunities, reps, stats, OSINT tools, and call logging
- `backend/database.py` — SQLite schema + sync query layer
- `backend/ingest.py` — One-time script to import processed JSON into SQLite with scoring + pitch generation
- `backend/straightline.db` — 119k listings + 357k pre-scored opportunities

## Data

Source data lives in `data/raw/` (Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, Virginia SCC). Run `npm run data:build` to regenerate processed JSON from raw sources, then `cd backend && python3 ingest.py` to reload the DB.

## What changed

- Replaced 115MB browser-loaded JSON with paginated SQLite backend
- Every lead now carries 1–3 pre-crafted Tech Pros pitch opportunities:
  - **$100 Logo → Website Deal** (starter site for businesses with no web presence)
  - **AI Employee Setup** (chatbot + scheduler for service businesses)
  - **Local SEO Domination** (rank in Hampton Roads search)
  - **Social Ads + Content System** (Meta/TikTok for consumer-facing businesses)
  - **CRM + Pipeline Setup** (close more leads in 90 days)
  - **Full Digital Presence Package** (bundle everything)
- Opportunities view now shows deal value, close probability, and one-click actions
- Call interactions write back to the database
- Floor view loads 250 listings at a time via API

## OSINT Toolkit

The backend integrates **27 native Parrot OS Security Edition tools** across 8 categories:

| Category | Tools | Ready |
|----------|-------|-------|
| Domain Intel | whois, dig, dnsrecon, nslookup, host, dnsenum, sublist3r | 7/7 |
| Web Recon | whatweb, wafw00f, nikto, curl/http_headers | 4/4 |
| SSL / TLS | openssl/ssl_cert, sslyze, testssl.sh | 2/3 |
| Network | ping, traceroute, nmap, masscan | 4/4 |
| Dir / Brute | gobuster, dirb, ffuf, feroxbuster | 4/4 |
| People / OSINT | sherlock, theharvester, holehe | 1/3 |
| SMB / AD | enum4linux, smbclient, netexec, ldapsearch | 4/4 |
| Vuln Scan | sqlmap | 1/1 |

### Missing tools to install on your Parrot OS machine
```bash
sudo apt install theharvester testssl.sh
pip3 install holehe
```

### Recommended additional toolkit
```bash
sudo apt install amass assetfinder findomain nuclei
pip3 install dalfox sn0int photon maigret
```

See `backend/osint-toolkit-plan.md` for the full expansion plan.

Outcome-based sessions, not generic advice:

offer/positioning review · first-users strategy · growth audit · newsletter growth call.

1. **Launch & distribution** — launch plan, first-users, growth audit
2. **Landing page / positioning** — teardown, offer/positioning review
3. **Founder content / X growth** — X strategy, newsletter growth call

## How a session works (productized)

1. **Pre-call intake** — tell us what you're stuck on; we match you with the right builder

We vet for proof, not polish:
- Proof of work
- Real audience or traction
- Clear niche skill
- Specific outcomes they can help with
- No fake "guru" energy (no income screenshots, no guaranteed-results promises)

It begins with an introduction to Rust data structures and algorithms and covers the entire spectrum, including memory safety, type system, concurrency, and other features of Rust 2018. ## What you will learn * Design and implement complex data structures in Rust * Create and use well-tested and reusable components with Rust * Understand the basics of multithreaded programming and advanced algorithm design * Explore application profiling based on benchmarking and testing * Study and apply best practices and strategies in error handling * Create efficient web applications with the Actix-web framework * Use Diesel for type-safe database interactions in your web application ### Hardware requirements For an optimal student experience, we recommend the following hardware configuration: * **Processor**: 2.6 GHz or higher multi-core processor * **Memory**: 8GB RAM * **Hard disk**: 30GB or more * An Internet connection ### Software requirements You'll also need the following software installed: * Microsoft's Visual Studio Code (https://code.visualstudio.com/), arguably one of the best Rust code editors * Rust support for Visual Studio Code via a plugin (https://github.com/rust-lang/rls-vscode) * Rust Language Server (RLS), found at https://github.com/rust-lang/rls-vscode, installed via rustup (https://rustup.rs/) * Debugging support using the LLDB frontend plugin (https://github.com/vadimcn/vscode-lldb) for Visual Studio Code ### Download a free PDF If you have already purchased a print or Kindle version of this book, you can get a DRM-free PDF version at no cost.
